title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Deployment Guide, Reference Architectures, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended deployment guides for Private Deployments (VPC-hosted and on‑prem), reference architectures, packaging options, day‑2 operational guidance, and detailed upgrade & rollback procedures. It is intended for platform engineers, solutions engineers, and customer SREs who operate or onboard Private deployments.

Scope

- VPC-hosted (customer VPC with Redwood Private control plane connectivity)
- On‑prem / air‑gapped packaging and install
- Hybrid architectures (control plane hosted, data plane in customer network)
- Day‑2 operations: monitoring, backups, scaling, incident playbooks
- Upgrade and rollback: safe canary and blue/green patterns and verification checks

Audience

Platform teams, customer SREs, Redwood solutions engineers, and security/compliance reviewers.

Ownership and Contacts

- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments team
- Oncall alias: eng-private-deployments-oncall@redwood.ai
- Escalation: PagerDuty (Primary: eng-platform, Secondary: eng-sre)

High‑Level Reference Architectures

1) VPC‑Hosted (Recommended for cloud customers)

- Components: redwood-control-plane (managed by Redwood), redwood-data-plane (customer VPC), redwood-proxy, ingress (NGINX or ALB), cert-manager, HashiCorp Vault (optional), KMS integration.
- Network: Private subnets for workers, NAT/egress for image pulls (or replicate images to ECR/GCR), restricted control-plane egress to Redwood endpoints over TLS.
- Security: Customer IAM roles for node pools, security groups limiting access to control plane IPs, and mTLS between proxy and workers.
- Sizing guidance: 1 worker (8 vCPU, 64GB RAM, 1xA10/A100-40GB) supports ~400 concurrent small generations (<=128 tokens) under batching.
- SLO targets: 99.9% availability, p95 request latency <= 150ms for 512 token responses on dedicated GPU pools.

2) On‑Prem / Air‑Gapped (Regulated environments)

- Components packaged as container images and operator manifests (Helm + kustomize) with an offline bundle for images and charts.
- Control plane: Customer-managed control plane option or offline control plane image that runs in customer network.
- Secrets: Integrations with customer HSM/KMS (KMIP or PKCS11) and optional Vault connector.
- Storage: NFS or Ceph recommended for shared model artifact storage; local NVMe for KV cache/LLM runtime.
- Hardware: GPU nodes must match supported driver/cuda versions; we publish validated combos in quantization-profiles.

3) Hybrid (Control plane in Redwood, data plane in customer network)

- Use when customers require minimal on‑prem control-plane footprint but have regulatory constraints on inference data.
- All traffic from data plane to control plane is over mutual TLS with strict token scope.
- Default fallback: model inference executed locally, metadata/telemetry forwarded on opt‑in basis.

Customer Requirements Library (Prerequisites checklist)

Network and DNS

- Allowlisted outbound IP ranges to Redwood control plane (see related pages for current list).
- DNS entries for ingress (e.g., redwood.example.internal) and wildcard certs for internal services.

IAM & Access

- Kubernetes cluster with admin-level bootstrap for installation.
- Cloud: dedicated node pools and service account with minimal privileges for worker nodes.

Storage & Hardware

- GPU requirements: listed driver, CUDA, and OS compatibility matrix (see quantization-profiles).
- Persistent volumes: recommended 1 TB NVMe per GPU for runtime cache and 10 TB distributed storage for model artifacts (size varies by models served).

Security & Compliance

- KMS/HSM integration plan and audit logging retention requirements.
- Network egress policy: whether telemetry is allowed to Redwood or must be proxied.

Packaging and Installation Options

1) Air‑gapped bundle

- Contents: OCI images tarball, Helm charts, kustomize overlays, offline installers (install.sh), signed checksums, and verification keys.
- Installation flow (high level):
  1. Validate prerequisites (hardware, storage, kernel drivers).
  2. Load images into local registry: docker load / ctr images import -> tag -> push to local registry.
  3. Apply kustomize overlays for customer-specific networking.
  4. Create secrets for KMS/HSM and TLS certs.
  5. Run install.sh which invokes Helm with customer overlays.

2) Online install (recommended for VPC)

- Uses ArgoCD or Helm with imagePullSecrets for cloud registries.
- Install steps:
  1. Apply namespace and RBAC manifests.
  2. Deploy control plane connectors and service accounts.
  3. Deploy data-plane components and configure autoscaling policies.
  4. Validate health checks and perform smoke test (see Verification section).

3) Kubernetes manifests and operators

- We provide a redwood-operator CRD to manage lifecycle of model serving deployments, autoscaling, and quantization profiles. Include example CR below.

Deployment Example (CR snippet)

```yaml
apiVersion: redwood.ai/v1
kind: ModelDeployment
metadata:
  name: semantic-search-small
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  model: rwd/llama-3-7b
  replicas: 2
  resources:
    gpu: nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    cpu: "8"
    memory: "64Gi"
  batching:
    max_batch_size: 64
    max_latency_ms: 50
  cache:
    kv_cache_size_gb: 32
```

Verification & Smoke Tests

- Health endpoints: /healthz, /ready, /metrics on cluster-internal services.
- Smoke test script (recommended): run a 10-request load with model rwd/compat-test and assert p95 latency < configured threshold and successful response rate = 100%.

Day‑2 Operations: Monitoring, Backups, and Scaling

Monitoring and Observability

- Recommended stack: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki for logs, Tempo/Jaeger for tracing, and Alertmanager for alerts.
- Key metrics to monitor:
  - inference_requests_total (per-model)
  - inference_latency_seconds (p50, p95, p99)
  - gpu_utilization_percent (per-node) - alert if > 95% sustained for 5m
  - batch_queue_length - alert if > 100 for 2m
  - disk_free_percent - alert if < 15%
  - kv_cache_hit_rate - target > 75% for production workloads

Alerting thresholds (recommendation)

- P95 latency breach: p95 > 2x baseline for 5 minutes -> SEV2
- Error rate: 5xx rate > 1% of requests in 5 minutes -> SEV1
- GPU memory OOMs: any OOM -> SEV1

Runbooks (examples)

1) High 5xx Rate

- Symptoms: increase in inference 5xx, error traces in proxy and worker logs.
- Steps:
  1. Check rolling restarts: kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide.
  2. Inspect worker logs: kubectl logs <worker-pod> -c inference-runtime.
  3. If OOM observed, scale up replicas or reduce batch sizes.
  4. If config/regression suspected, rollback last config change (see Upgrade section).
  5. Escalate to eng-sre on SEV1.

2) Slow P95 Latency

- Steps:
  1. Check batch_queue_length and batch sizes.
  2. Verify GPU utilization; if low and CPU high, investigate I/O.
  3. Consider enabling prefix caching or increasing max_batch_size per workload.

Backup and Restore

- Model artifacts: daily snapshot to customer-approved object store (S3/GCS or on‑prem equivalent).
- Config/Etcd: weekly etcd snapshot + offsite transfer for HA clusters.
- Recovery test: quarterly restore drill for at least one non-production cluster.

Scaling Guidelines

- Horizontal scaling: prefer adding worker replicas for stateless frontends, but ensure KV cache warms are considered.
- Vertical scaling: updating GPU type requires draining and redeploying nodes — schedule during maintenance window.

Upgrade and Rollback Procedures

General principles

- All upgrades must be tested in staging that mirrors customer topology (network, KMS integrations).
- Use canary or blue/green strategies. Always maintain a rollback plan with known good image/tag.
- Record a snapshot of config, k8s manifests, and etcd before upgrade.

Canary upgrade (recommended for minor releases)

1. Build and sign release images.
2. Deploy new version to 5% of worker capacity (label nodes/cordon).
3. Run synthetic load tests against canary: 1K requests or 10 minutes of steady traffic.
4. Validate metrics: p95 latency within 1.2x baseline, error rate <0.1%.
5. If green, ramp to 25% for 15 minutes, then to 50% and finally 100% with monitoring windows at each step.
6. If metrics regress at any step, immediately stop rollouts and execute rollback.

Blue/Green (recommended for major or stateful changes)

1. Deploy new control-plane version into a new namespace or cluster (green).
2. Mirror configuration and secrets to green environment.
3. Route a subset of traffic using service mesh or ingress weight (e.g., Istio or NGINX canary weights).
4. Run smoke tests and acceptance tests.
5. On success, switch 100% traffic and decommission previous (blue) after a retention window.

Rollback checklist

- Keep the last good image tag and Helm release name.
- Restore etcd snapshot if control plane schema changed.
- Validate DNS and certs post-rollback.
- Notify customer and relevant owners.

Post‑Upgrade Verification

- Run the smoke test script and a real workload replay for at least 30 minutes.
- Check telemetry for anomalies: spike in errors, changed latency distribution, or telemetry gaps.

Common Failure Modes and Mitigations

- GPU driver mismatch: Validate driver/kernel before upgrade; rollback node driver update if required.
- Model artifact corruption during sync: verify checksums in snapshot/restore.
- KMS connectivity issues post-upgrade: ensure network routes and certs for KMS are intact and test key-wrap/unwrap flows.

Appendix A: Configuration Table (example)

| Component | Default | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| p95 latency target | 150ms | 100–200ms | depends on model and token length |
| kv_cache_size_gb | 16 | 32 | increase for low latency workloads |
| autoscale.min_replicas | 2 | 2 | avoid single-replica inference workers |
| autoscale.max_replicas | 20 | 20–200 | set based on license and GPU pool size |

Appendix B: Sample CLI snippets

- Install (online)

```bash
# create namespace and RBAC
kubectl apply -f rwd-namespace.yaml
# install operator
helm repo add redwood https://packages.redwood.ai/charts
helm install rwd-operator redwood/redwood-operator -n redwood --set image.tag=2027.03.0
```

- Load offline images (air‑gapped)

```bash
tar xzf redwood-airgap-2027-03-01.tar.gz
./load-images-to-registry.sh --registry registry.internal:5000 --bundle ./images
```

Appendix C: Acceptance Test Checklist

1. All pods in redwood namespace are Ready.
2. /healthz and /ready endpoints return HTTP 200.
3. Synthetic workload p95 latency within threshold.
4. Model artifacts validated via checksum.
5. Alerting rules evaluated and test alerts exercised.
